newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex ends off sharply in correction.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex ends off sharply in correction.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures prices ended sharply lower Tuesday after traders returned from a long weekend to find a market bulging with speculative long positions, a clear signal to sell, traders said.
Unleaded gasoline and heating oil prices also tumbled.
July crude oil lost 84 cents to settle at $20.79 a barrel, after dropping to a low of $20.65 from its high of $21.57, where it opened.
July unleaded gasoline ended at 63.00 cents a gallon, off 1.90 cents. July heating oil fell 2.26 cents, settling at 55.22 cents a gallon.

A surge in speculative long positions in crude oil over the last two weeks - turning the market to a net long position - was recorded in Friday's CFTC Commitment of Traders report, but with many players out of the market early ahead of the long weekend, many were caught offguard.

"I would never have guessed this market was that long," said Bob MacMinn, president of Toronto-based MPAS. "I think it was a big surprise for a lot of people, and I think that had a big impact" on Tuesday's dealings.

The huge long side of the market left traders wondering who was left to buy the market, and when the liquidation would come. They would acknowledge later in the session that "today" was probably the right answer to the latter question.
Aside from the current volatility that traders have pegged to funds and other speculators, lurking in the background is the perception that the market's fundamentals are growing consistently weaker.
Neither crude oil inventories nor refinery capacity utilization rates are expected to have declined significantly from last week's levels, traders said Tuesday.

Crude markets typically look for demand in the unleaded gasoline market during peak summer driving periods, and although unleaded gasoline inventories are about 7 million barrels below last year's levels, crude inventories and refinery capacity utilization continue to remain high.

"A lot depends on what products do, and right now the products are coming off. Unless gasoline can take the ball and run with it, over time the fundamentals are less favorable," said Smith Barney analyst John Saucer.

Profit margins have begun to decline significantly in Asia and Europe, which has caused some major refiners to begin scaling back production, a development that does not bode well for the industry's expectations of upcoming demand.
"When all is said and done, margins really determine" the relative health of the products markets, Saucer said.

July crude oil futures breached a succession of key chart points during its decline Tuesday, including the 10-day moving average of $21.61 and the 20-day moving average of $20.81, where support was expected to be strong.
The next key technical support level for July crude was seen in the area of $20.50.
